summary: SpaceX and Anthropic IPOs will unlock significant mutual fund buying power for private AI markets
summary_extended: Baker argues that the anticipated IPOs of SpaceX and Anthropic will paradoxically unlock new institutional buying power for private AI markets rather than simply converting private holdings to public ones. The mechanism is regulatory: US mutual funds face strict limits on the percentage of illiquid/private assets they can hold, and their current SpaceX and Anthropic positions are consuming that capacity. Once these companies go public and their shares become liquid and fully unlocked, mutual funds will free up room under their illiquid asset caps to redeploy into other private AI companies. Baker frames this as an underappreciated structural dynamic — the IPOs are not just liquidity events for existing holders but catalysts that expand the total addressable institutional capital available to private AI markets. He presents this as a medium-term, contrarian observation about capital flows that most market participants are not pricing in.
